column2: AI education North America 2026 adoption regulation players
column4: US state level is where the binding rules are: 134 AI-in-education bills across 31 states in 2026. California AB 1159 restricts training models on student data; Idaho SB 1227 requires privacy protections for school AI tools; Oklahoma + Maryland require human oversight and bar AI from high-stakes decisions about students; Georgia + Mississippi add AI content to CS credits. Federal: K-12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 (H.R. 8747) advanced in a July markup. Districts: NYC one-year moratorium on student-facing AI through grade 8; Katy ISD (TX) bans GenAI chatbots K-6 with supervised phase-in to 12. Canada: "AI for All" national strategy launched 2026-06-04, AI literacy push, NO legislative date. Mexico: bills, no regulator. Adoption: 60% of US K-12 teachers used AI in 2024-25, 32% at least weekly. 🔴 The "North America = 36% of global market" figure is aggregator-sourced and NOT published

column2: AI education EMEA 2026 adoption regulation players
column3: 🟢 REAL, and the regulatory clock is the story
column4: EU AI Act: systems that evaluate learners or influence access to qualifications are HIGH-RISK, requiring conformity assessment and human oversight. 🔴 DATE CONFLICT IN THE SOURCES — one guide says high-risk obligations apply from Aug 2026, the Commission's own milestones page lists 31 July 2026 entry into force and 27 July 2026 for the AI Omnibus. Recorded as a conflict, NOT resolved, because the authoritative text is not reachable (see curriculum-authority-egress). Member states (OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026): Czechia embeds GenAI in mandatory digital competence; France teaches AI literacy via the Pix platform; Lithuania preparing a NATIONAL REGISTER OF APPROVED AI TOOLS + teacher competence frameworks; Finland's national agency has issued GenAI recommendations. 🔴 Market figure ($2.64B 2026, 31.9% CAGR to $8.0B 2030, Finland/Estonia/Netherlands leading K-12) is VENDOR-STYLE and NOT published. 🟡 The EMEA VENDOR gap p288 declared is STILL OPEN: this leg again returned only regulators and standards bodies

column2: AI education APAC 2026 adoption regulation players
column3: 🟢 REAL, and education is NAMED high-risk in a binding law
column4: South Korea AI Basic Act in force 2026-01-22 with its enforcement decree, including adoption supports (public data sharing, R&D, standardisation, SME/startup support). 🔴 VIETNAM IS THE FINDING: its AI law names EDUCATION as one of six high-risk sectors, explicitly including AUTOMATED ASSESSMENT and BEHAVIOURAL MONITORING; compliance by 2027-03-01, with systems already operating before 2026-08-15 getting a further six months. 🔴 Effective dates VARY ACROSS SOURCES (one says the law took effect 2026-03-01) — carried as a conflict, not a fact. China: mandatory registration, content labelling, penalties to CNY 50M. Taiwan AI Basic Act passed Dec 2025. Singapore + Japan: voluntary guidelines over existing law. Players per a commercial report: Google, Microsoft, IBM, Pearson, Byju's; China/India/Japan dominant. 🔴 NO education-specific APAC adoption statistics in the leg

column2: AI education LATAM 2026 adoption regulation players
column3: 🟢 REAL, strongest ADOPTION data of any region this pass
column4: UNESCO IESALC (with UNU-IAS) surveyed 200 higher-education institutions across 19 countries: 87% use AI in at least one area, 74% in teaching and learning — and only 26% have a FORMAL AI STRATEGY. 1 in 2 students reports confusion about appropriate AI use. TALIS 2024 secondary teachers reporting AI use: Brazil 56%, Chile 55%, Colombia 53%, Costa Rica 52%, against an OECD average of 36% — LATAM is ABOVE the OECD average on teacher adoption. Ceibal (Uruguay): 75% of public-school teachers report using these tools. Digital Education Council LATAM survey 2026: 30,000+ responses across 29 institutions. CENIA + ECLAC: regional AI investment averages SIX TIMES LOWER than the global one. 🔴 NO binding national or regional AI-in-education rule found — governance is voluntary/institutional, with UNESCO's 2021 ethics recommendation the main reference. The adoption-vs-governance GAP is the regional finding
